newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March S&P 500 stages late recovery, ends up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March S&P 500 stages late recovery, ends up.

text.p: U.S. March Standard and Poor's 500 futures finished slightly higher after a frenzy of late short-covering cut steep losses.

U.S. stock index futures began the new year with huge losses after strong U.S. data, then languished amid nervous and choppy trade before powering higher late. Traders said waves of local short-covering and dealer buying sparked the late recovery.
"I know everybody was getting loaded up on the downside and then they got caught short," an S&P 500 trader said. "It was an interesting day."

March Standard and Poor's 500 futures initially rallied the opening five-point limit before backing off heading into the National Association of Purchasing Management report. When the overall index came in stronger than expected, March S&Ps collapsed to trade more than 11 points lower in brisk trading.
The NAPM's December index rose to 54.0 from 52.7 in November.
March chopped around and traded mid-range for much of the session until T-bond futures closed. Then March S&Ps made another run for the session low, failed, and promptly rebounded.
"It seemed to coincide with the bond close. They took one more run at the downside and then they took it up and never looked back," he said.

"We just overdid it for the last few days," another S&P 500 futures trader said. Once the market began correcting from the steep losses, short-covering in somewhat thin pits accelerated the recovery, he said.
"This is a good sign. I like the fact that we bounced like this," one S&P trader said. "But again, it's not a true picture because I think a lot of guys are still out."
March volume was estimated at 87,000 contracts, he said.

At settlement, March S&P 500 futures were up 0.20 points to 744.70, Russell 2000s rose 2.25 points to 365.00, Value Line futures rallied 2.00 points to 685.00 and Nikkei 225 index futures eased 100.0 to 19,280.0.
